def _get_item_length(item, parents_ids=frozenset([])):
    """
    Get the length of an item by counting all its elements recursively.
    Handles circular references by tracking parent object ids.
    """
    item_id = id(item)
    
    # Avoid infinite loops from circular references
    if item_id in parents_ids:
        return 0
    
    # For immutable types that don't contain other objects, return 1
    if isinstance(item, (str, bytes, int, float, bool, type(None))):
        return 1
    
    # Add current item to parents_ids for circular reference detection
    new_parents_ids = add_to_frozen_set(parents_ids, item_id)
    
    length = 1  # Count the item itself
    
    try:
        if isinstance(item, Mapping):
            # For dicts and dict-like objects
            for key, value in item.items():
                length += _get_item_length(key, new_parents_ids)
                length += _get_item_length(value, new_parents_ids)
        elif isinstance(item, (list, tuple)):
            # For lists and tuples
            for sub_item in item:
                length += _get_item_length(sub_item, new_parents_ids)
        elif isinstance(item, set):
            # For sets
            for sub_item in item:
                length += _get_item_length(sub_item, new_parents_ids)
        elif isinstance(item, np_ndarray):
            # For numpy arrays
            length += item.size
        elif hasattr(item, '__dict__'):
            # For custom objects with __dict__
            for key, value in item.__dict__.items():
                length += _get_item_length(value, new_parents_ids)
    except (TypeError, AttributeError):
        # If we can't iterate, just return 1
        pass
    
    return length
